get.description: Returns audit-log entries for a single model, newest first. Use the filters to narrow by event type, actor, deployment, environment, source, or time window, and the cursor to page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous page. Omit to fetch the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return per page. Defaults to 20, and must be between 1 and 200.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Sort order by the time the action occurred. Defaults to DESC (newest first). Ignored when paginating with a cursor.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against resource names and IDs in the entry.

parameters.name: event_type_groups
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries whose event type falls in one of these groups.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries whose acting user is one of these IDs.

parameters.name: deployment_ids
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries referencing one of these model deployment IDs.

parameters.name: chain_deployment_ids
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries referencing one of these chain deployment IDs.

parameters.name: environment_names
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries for one of these environments.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: When set, returns only entries issued from one of these surfaces.

parameters.name: start_epoch_millis
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds for the start of the window. Defaults to the beginning of the audit-log history.

parameters.name: end_epoch_millis
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds for the end of the window. Defaults to the current time.

)

print(response.text)

get.description: Gets all the logs for a model deployment in the given time range, which defaults to the last 30 minutes. A failed or older deployment may only have logs from before that window; pass `start_epoch_millis` to widen it back to the build/deploy time.

parameters.name: start_epoch_millis
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds at which to start fetching logs. Defaults to 30 minutes before the end. The window from start to end must not exceed 7 days.

parameters.name: end_epoch_millis
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds at which to stop fetching logs. Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Sort order for logs

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit of logs to fetch in a single request

parameters.name: min_level
parameters.description: Minimum log severity to include. Omit to return all log lines, including lines that have no level. Any explicit value returns lines at or above that severity and drops lines without a level.

parameters.name: replica
parameters.description: Only return logs emitted by this replica (5-char short ID).

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Only return logs tagged with this inference request ID.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Only return logs from this component.

parameters.name: search_pattern
parameters.description: RE2 regular expression matched against the log message. Prefer `includes` and `excludes` for plain substring matches.

parameters.name: includes
parameters.description: Case-sensitive substrings that must all appear in the log message.

parameters.name: excludes
parameters.description: Case-sensitive substrings; lines containing any of these are dropped.

DeploymentPatchPointV1.description:
A patch point: the source state the next patch is computed against.

The content hash that identifies a point is derived from this state (see
`DeploymentPatchPointWithHashV1.hash`), so a request only sends the state and
the server stamps the hash. A previous point's hash plus the current local
source is enough to compute the next patch, so the watch client reads the
point it is patching off of.

content_hashes.description: Map of every non-ignored source path, relative and forward-slash, to its content hash: files map to the hex blake3 digest of their bytes, directories map to null. This is the full signature of the source tree and what the content hash is derived from.

DeploymentPatchPointWithHashV1.description:
A patch point plus its server-assigned content hash, returned in responses.

Requests omit the hash (the server derives it from the source state); responses
include it so the watch client can echo it back as the next patch's
`prev_patch_hash` without having to recompute the fold itself.

content_hashes.description: Map of every non-ignored source path, relative and forward-slash, to its content hash: files map to the hex blake3 digest of their bytes, directories map to null. This is the full signature of the source tree and what the content hash is derived from.
content_hashes.title: Content Hashes

config.description: The verbatim config.yaml text for this source state.
config.title: Config

requirements.description: Requirements resolved from the config's requirements file, when it points at one. Empty when requirements are declared inline in the config.
requirements.title: Requirements

hash.description: Content hash identifying this exact source state, and the link patches build on. It is derived deterministically from `content_hashes`, so a request need not send it - the server derives it. It is derived by sorting the `content_hashes` keys as paths, splitting each key on '/' into its path components and ordering the keys by comparing those component lists element by element, each component compared by Unicode code point (equivalently UTF-8 byte order). Treating '/' as a path separator this way, rather than as the ordinary character U+002F, means a key that is an ancestor path sorts before a sibling whose name extends the first differing component (so e.g. 'a/b' sorts before 'a.b'). A blake3 hasher is then built, and for each key in that order updated with the blake3 digest (32 raw bytes) of the key encoded as UTF-8, then, when the entry is a file (non-null value), with that file's digest as 32 raw bytes. The stream uses raw digest bytes, but the values in `content_hashes` are those digests hex-encoded (64 hex chars), so decode each value from hex first. Directory entries (null value) contribute only their key digest. The result is the hasher's own hex digest.
hash.title: Hash

list is the index used to read that metric out of each value set's ``values``.

or volume by status). ``label_sets`` enumerates those series in order; each

- ``SECONDS``: a duration in seconds.

- ``MEBIBYTES``: a size in mebibytes (MiB).
- ``COUNT``: a dimensionless tally of discrete things.
- ``RATIO``: a dimensionless ratio. Usually in ``[0, 1]`` but may exceed 1
  (e.g. CPU usage in cores = cpu-seconds/second).
- ``CELSIUS``: a temperature in degrees Celsius.

A stage of a replica startup.

- ``SCHEDULING``: waiting for the replica to be placed on a node.
- ``IMAGE_PULL``: pulling the container image.
- ``WEIGHT_DOWNLOAD``: downloading model weights.
- ``CONTAINER_CREATE``: creating and starting the model container, including
  ``CONTAINER_START`` and ``READINESS``.
- ``CONTAINER_START``: starting the model container.
- ``READINESS``: waiting for the model to pass its readiness check.
